newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: One killed, nearly 100 hurt in Bangladesh strike.
newsitem.headline: One killed, nearly 100 hurt in Bangladesh strike.

text.p: One person died and nearly 100 people were injured by violence during an eight-hour opposition-led general strike which disrupted Bangladesh on Sunday.

Police said one unidentified person died and over 40 were hurt when the engine and a passenger coach of a train ran off tracks that had been damaged by unknown attackers at Hasimpur, 32 km (20 miles) from the port of Chittagong.
Witnesses said the attackers tore away about 100 yards (metres) of train lines but the driver could not see it because of early morning fog.
Seven others were injured in bomb explosions in the port city, where police arrested at least 10 BNP pickets, witnesses said.

In Dhaka, former home (interior) minister Abdul Matin Chowdhury, leading a group of pickets, was hit by a stone while passing by offices of the ruling Awami League. He was taken to hospital bleeding from the head, witnesses said.
The dawn-to-afternoon strike, called by the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, shut businesses and kept transport off the roads.
Strike enforcers, many carrying sticks and wearing headbands, marched on the streets of Dhaka, and set off dozens of home-made bombs and firecrackers, witnesses said.
They said strike supporters and opponents fought running battles in Dhaka's Mirpur area, where nearly 10 people were injured.
Riot police and para-military forces patrolled streets and guarded key installations.
Officials in Chittagong said the strike shut everything including the port. The coutry's two bourses in Dhaka and Chittagong were also closed.

Other main cities including Khulna, Rajshahi, Sylhet, Netrokona, Mymensingh, Chandpur, Comilla, Feni, Rangpur and Dinajpur also witnessed strike-related violence which wounded some 30 people, local reporters said.
Rail and air traffic operated but with fewer passengers, transport officials said.
In Dhaka, hundred of government employees either walked to their offices or took pedal rickshaws, which operated in defiance of the strike. Many senior officials stayed in their offices overnight.
The BNP called the stoppage for Sunday, a working day in mainly Moslem Bangladesh, in its first major attempt to destabilise the eight-month-old government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Hasina took office last June following a general election in which the BNP accused Hasina's Awami League of vote-rigging, but which was billed as free and fair by local and international monitors.

The BNP says the strike is to protest what it views as the government's failure to provide the basic needs of people in this poor nation and against Hasina's warmer ties with rival India, which the BNP sees as a plot to surrender Bangladeshi sovereignty.
